 Significant number of train services cancelled or disrupted this weekend while works are carried out 
 Dublin commuter trains will be worst affected, with a large portion of the soutside Dart line closed for three days. 
 7.25am, 22 Oct 2026 
 5.2k 
 Share options 
 Copy link
 Email
 Facebook
 X
 A SIGNIFICANT NUMBER of train services will be disrupted this weekend due to engineering works that must be carried out.
 Dublin commuter trains will be worst affected, with a large portion of the southside Dart line closed for three days.
 Rail Users Ireland, an advocacy group for passengers, has said that while the disruption is no doubt frustrating for those who had plans for the bank holiday, the works are essential for the maintenance of the rail system.
 Advertisement 
 Limerick 
 Engineering works will take place between Limerick and Limerick Junction on Saturday 24, Sunday 25 and Monday 26 October.
 Services between Limerick and Dublin Heuston will also be disrupted.
 Some journeys have been cancelled, while others will be replaced by buses.
 Details for specific services can be found here .
 On Monday 26 October, a few services between Waterford and Limerick Junction are cancelled. They are as follows:
 07.20am Waterford to Limerick Junction
 4:25pm Waterford to Limerick Junction
 09.45am Limerick Junction to Waterford 
 6.40pm Limerick Junction to Waterford
 Dart services
 There will be no Dart service between Grand Canal Dock and Bray, and Howth Junction and Donaghmede, on Saturday, Sunday or Monday, due to engineering works on that part of the line.
 Trains will only go between Malahide and Grand Canal Dock .
 The following Dart stations will be closed: Bayside, Sutton, Howth, Lansdowne Road, Sandymount, Sydney Parade, Booterstown, Blackrock, Seapoint, Salthill and Monkstown, Dún Laoghaire, Sandycove and Glasthule, Glenagerary, Dalkey, Killiney, Shankill and Woodbrook.
 Mark Gleeson of Rail Users Ireland said while the disruption is “not ideal”, it is necessary for the improvement of the lines.
 Roughly every 20 years certain wiring and tracks must be replaced. Additionally, the new fleet of commuter trains will have built in ramps so that people won’t have to ask an attendant at the station for one. The ramps will pop out onto the platform automatically. However, the height of some platforms have had to be changed to allow for this new feature.
 “This work is of a nature that it cannot be done overnight,” Gleeson said.
 “There isn’t enough time between half past midnight and 5.30 in the morning.”
